hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

In other words, the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector between any pair of corresponding points in the image and the pre-image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
Since the $x$-axis is *horizontal*, the reflection will move each point of quadrilateral $ABCD$ *vertically* across the axis.

For example, point $A$ is $4$ units above the $x$-axis, so $A'$ will be $4$ units below the axis.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Quadrilateral A B C D with point A at one, four, point B at negative four, two, point C at negative five, negative four, and point D at negative two, negative one. A dashed arrow points at both point A prime at one, negative four and point A.

hints.content:

A dashed arrow points at both point A prime at one, negative four and point A. A dashed arrow points at both point B prime at negative four, negative two and point B.
